structured_output.summary: Chunk `validation-policy` of phase 19 delivers the G25 response correction where the plan requires it: a single mode-aware relaxation in the shared bounded validator plus an explicit mode-aware graph node for operation contract selection. `crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1163-1171` bypasses exactly the eight named string-format assertions (uuid, rfc3339, datetime, date, duration, email, url, regex) plus generator-marked vendor-only `min`/`max` bounds in both response modes, keeps string type checks, limits, finite-JSON rules, refinements and defaults, leaves `Mode::Request` untouched, and fails closed on unknown check kinds (`_ => false`); I confirmed no other string check kinds exist in the shipped graph, so the bypass list is complete rather than partial. Operation selection is explicit, not name-inferred: `tools/red_team_dataplane.py:337-340` emits a `ZodResponseCompatibility` node per paired operation whose `request` branch is the retained strict vendor root and whose `response` branch is the actual frozen TypeScript root (with explicit array/opaque wrappers), and `response_baselines` fails closed on ambiguous mappings, unclassified expressions and any drift from 36 pairs. Vendor string bounds are marked `requestOnly` at generation time (`:241`), the frozen graph is proven byte-identical after merge (`tools/test_red_team_dataplane.py:49-58`), and all response transports (buffered, one_of, streaming) route through `options.response_mode()`. Evidence is real and executed, not claimed: the recorded checks at the reviewed SHA show 17 commands at exit 0, including both oracles, generator/audit freshness checks and `cargo fmt/check/clippy/test/doc` on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 (162s/177s) with `test result: ok … 0 failed` for `g25_response_compatibility`, `schema_contracts` and `red_team_vendor_models_generated`. Independence holds: `tools/schema-oracle.mts:215-251` and `tools/g25-oracle.mts:31-73` compute expectations by executing real Zod (importing the frozen `.local/typescript` schemas) and AJV on policy-adapted schemas, with self-invariants that throw if a format/enum mutation is rejected or if the oracle narrows TypeScript, and with env/fetch lockdown. Rust then asserts exact agreement across 60,271 frozen cases × three modes and 15,381 vendor cases × both response modes, every format node in the graph, and end-to-end typed clients preserving `job-1`/`p-1`/`map-1` and both reported timestamp forms. I verified the floor is genuinely exercised (outcomes contain many `strict:false, typescript:true, response:true` rows, and presence mutations are generated for every property). Remaining issues are medium/low and documentary or test-coverage shaped: the regenerated independent-corpus provenance string still omits the new format bypass, the generation guard skips verifying array/opaque wrapper targets (an `z.unknown()` vs passthrough-object flip would likely go untested), and the compatibility report does not disclose or quantify that the exclusive baseline floor rejects some documents the pinned vendor contract accepts. No blocker/high findings.

findings.description: The oracle's self-describing response policy (emitted as `policies.response` and committed at contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json:629) still lists only the pre-existing adaptations: "preserve unknown object fields; widen enum/string-literal-union vocabularies; preserve required types, individual literals, catchalls, refinements, defaults and transforms." It does not mention that tools/schema-oracle.mts:231 now strips the eight string-format checks (uuid, datetime, email, url, regex, date, duration, rfc3339) before executing Zod. The provenance of a 60,271-case corpus whose response expectations changed therefore understates the adaptation, and a future reader cannot tell from the artifact that formats are ignored.
findings.required_fix: Extend the `policies.response` string in tools/schema-oracle.mts:377 to state the exact set of bypassed string-format check kinds (and that frozen min/max bounds are retained), then regenerate contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json with `tools/schema-oracle.mts` and re-run the `--check` guard.

findings.description: `test_each_existing_operation_has_an_explicit_mode_switch` only asserts the wrapper's response target when `baseline['root']` is set and `not baseline['array']`, so the array and opaque baselines (7 of the 36 paired operations: 4 `z.array(...)`, 2 `z.unknown()`, 1 `z.object({}).passthrough()`) are never checked. The opaque wrappers built at tools/red_team_dataplane.py:335 differ materially (`ZodUnknown` accepts scalars, the passthrough object requires an object), and the g25 corpus only mutates property paths (`tools/g25_fixtures.py:58`), so a flipped or misbuilt opaque/array wrapper would not be caught by any current guard or regression.
findings.required_fix: Extend the guard to assert, for array baselines, that `nodes[wrapper['response']['$ref']]` is `ZodArray` whose `element.$ref == baseline['root']`, and for opaque baselines that the node is exactly `ZodUnknown` for `z.unknown()` and the passthrough `ZodObject` with a `ZodNever` catchall for `z.object({}).passthrough()`; optionally add root-level scalar/object cases for those roots to the g25 corpus.

findings.description: The report documents retaining baseline requiredness/nullability/types "instead of imposing stricter vendor fields", but does not disclose the opposite direction that exclusive baseline selection creates: contracts/compatibility/g25/outcomes.json contains multiple `{"strict":true,"typescript":false,"response":false}` rows, i.e. documents the pinned vendor 0.93.0 contract accepts that the shipped response validation now rejects for paired operations. Given that this patch exists because over-strict response validation broke a consumer, this residual risk should be stated and quantified rather than left derivable only from the raw corpus.
findings.required_fix: Add an explicit paragraph (and a generated count, with a few example operation/field paths, computed from contracts/compatibility/g25/outcomes.json in tools/g25_report.py) stating that the frozen baseline is used exclusively in response modes and can reject vendor-permitted documents, so that the retained strictness is an acknowledged, measured decision.

findings.description: `ZodNativeEnum` is widened unconditionally to `union(schema, string, number)`, which is looser than the Rust rule (a string is accepted only if the enum has string members, a number only if it has numeric members) and looser than the sibling oracle at tools/schema-oracle.mts:220-225. Likewise line 46 maps `ZodDiscriminatedUnion` to a plain `z.union`, dropping the exactly-one-success rule the validator enforces for `preserveUnknownResponse` nodes with an absent discriminator (crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:680-695). Where the oracle is looser than the implementation it cannot detect over-permissive Rust behavior.
findings.required_fix: Mirror the schema-oracle.mts native-enum type analysis in tools/g25-oracle.mts:36, and model discriminated unions with an exactly-one-match check (or record the deviation explicitly in the oracle's emitted policy text so the weaker expectation is auditable).

findings.description: The `responseOnly` presence check uses `self.mode == Mode::Request` rather than `!self.mode.is_response()`. `Mode` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and already has three variants; a future non-response mode would silently stop enforcing presence for response-only optional wrappers, unlike every other policy branch in this function which tests `is_response()`.
findings.required_fix: Change the condition to `!self.mode.is_response()` so the check follows the same mode predicate used by the rest of the validator.
